core_obligations: Turn the field extension into a geometric connectedness statement: since k is separably algebraically closed, the extension k' is geometrically connected over k (proof lines 781-784).
Pass to schemes: by the affine case, Z = Spec(k') is geometrically connected over k (proof lines 785-786).

Identify the base change as a product and apply the component-bijection lemma: X_{k'} = Z x_k X, so the projection X_{k'} -> X has geometrically connected source factor and induces a bijection of connected components; in particular X is geometrically connected over k exactly when it is connected (proof lines 787-788).
proof_roadmap: Note that over a separably algebraically closed field every extension is geometrically connected (proof lines 781-784).
Convert this into geometric connectedness of the affine scheme Spec(k') over k (proof lines 785-786).
Write the base change as a product with Spec(k') and invoke the component-bijection lemma for projection from a geometrically connected factor (proof lines 787-788).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a separably algebraically closed base field k and any extension k'/k, the base change X_{k'} -> X induces a bijection of connected components, so that X is geometrically connected exactly when it is connected (statement lines 772-777). The proof is a three-step reduction, and its non-formal content is the recognition that the hypothesis on k is exactly what makes the extension k' geometrically connected, hence makes Z = Spec(k') a geometrically connected factor, after which X_{k'} = Z x_k X falls under the component-bijection lemma for projection from such a factor (proof lines 781-788). Both the algebra statement and the two scheme-theoretic lemmas are quoted; what is contributed here is the assembly. The claim is H2.
